old_caption: The video captures a butterfly in flight, approaching an orange flower amidst a field of similar blooms. The butterfly, with its wings displaying intricate patterns of black, white, and brown, moves toward the flower. It then lands on the flower and remains still, with its wings partially or fully closed. The background is softly blurred, emphasizing the vibrant orange petals and the green stems of the flowers. The gentle breeze causes the flowers to sway slightly, adding a dynamic element to the scene. The overall atmosphere is one of peaceful coexistence between the butterfly and its floral environment.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a butterfly perched on an orange flower amidst a field of similar blooms. The butterfly, with its wings spread wide, displays intricate patterns of black, white, and brown. Its delicate antennae twitch as it feeds on the nectar of the flower. The background is softly blurred, emphasizing the vibrant orange petals and the green stems of the flowers. As the camera pans slightly to the right, another butterfly comes into view, also feeding on a nearby flower. This second butterfly mirrors the first in its coloration and posture. The gentle breeze causes the flowers to sway slightly, adding a dynamic element to the otherwise tranquil setting. The overall atmosphere is one of peaceful coexistence between the butterflies and their floral environment.
caption: The video captures a shallow-focus outdoor scene set against a soft green-and-white bokeh backdrop. Several yellow daisy-like blooms sit low in the frame, and a small dark insect perches motionless on an orange flower near the middle. A black-and-white spotted butterfly with orange-brown wing edges is the moving subject. It is already airborne near the top as the clip opens, its wings alternately spreading wide and folding edge-on. It drifts leftward and downward through the air, flapping steadily, before settling onto a lower-left yellow bloom. From that point onward the butterfly remains perched there, rhythmically opening and closing its wings in a basking flutter. Its wings are sometimes fully spread and sometimes raised nearly vertical. Meanwhile the framing slowly shifts, carrying the perched butterfly and its flower toward the center while the orange flower slides toward the right edge.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
